programmes.show_description: Goodbye Stan: Sitcom about a bus driver and his conductor pal. Stan gets a job up north and decides to get himself sacked in order to earn an extra week's wages.
Your daily escape designed to calm the mind and encourage relaxation and reflection.
Shopping from home.
Affairs of the Heart: Classic British sitcom. Oliver is delighted when Simon's ex-wife Stephanie takes him under her wing, but her ex-husband is terrified that she intends to stay.
Hot Water: Enduring British sitcom about a bus driver and his conductor pal. Jack and the inspector attempt to fix a water heater.
Louise returns from holiday and throws the factory workers out of the B and B as Bob confronts her about blackmailing Viv. Katie asks Perdy to look after the baby when it is born.
Jonny is shocked when Katie tells him of her plot to cut Gray out of the baby's life. Pollard has a visit from a health and safety officer, and Louise attempts to apologise to Viv.
Liz hoodwinks Steve before dressing up and spending the evening with Harry. Claire discovers the house exchange could fall through, and Paul receives news from his solicitor.
Sceptical about Harry's new friendship, Dan lets slip to Steve about Liz's date. Building work gets under way at Tyrone and Molly's home, while Claire turns the tables on Sally.
Your Sudden Death Question: Lewis and Hathaway are called in when a top quiz competitor is found floating dead in the fountain of an Oxford college on a bank holiday weekend.
Midday Sun: Police drama series set in the 1960s. A family brings terror to the inhabitants of Aidensfield when their lost dog is discovered to have rabies.
Turn of the Tide: Police drama series set in the 1960s. Nick is called to Whitby to investigate a case of smuggling, and Kate has to break some difficult news.
Country Matters: Controversial plans to build a supermarket in Elverton-cum-Latterly lead to murder when a man is stabbed - can Barnaby and Jones uncover the killer?
Katie plans to have her baby in London and put it up for adoption, having conned money out of Grayson to do so. Gennie realises Chas fancies the hot new vet Josh.
Determined to prove her innocence, Liz decides to cool things off with Harry, while Sally and Claire both stand their ground. Paul contemplates a future away from the Street.
Jack discovers Paul's plans to flee Weatherfield, while Sally confronts Claire about her criticism of the house and Leanne arranges a rendezvous with Dan at the show flat.
Love Child: Police drama series set in the 1960s. A break-in at the local council offices leads to a more serious crime when an adoption file goes missing.
Nice Girls Don't: Police drama series set in Yorkshire in the 1960s. Gina undergoes a terrible ordeal that leaves her distressed by the attitude of the police and the local people.
Shot at Dawn: A long-running feud between two Midsomer Parva families that dates back to the First World War appears to escalate to murder after the unveiling of a war memorial.
When a body is found in a shallow grave in the shadow of the Glastonbury Tor, a sinister sequence of events is triggered that only DS Dodds can decipher.

Jonny and Paul argue about the situation between Katie, Gray and Perdy. Chas warns Gennie about turning into a layabout, and Sam offers to help Jo out on the farm for free.
Brenda catches Gennie in the hot tub with Eli and accuses the Dingles of corrupting her daughter. Diane comforts Gray, and Paul begs Jonny not to give up on their relationship.
The residents are terrorised by a gang of yobs who run riot on the Street, and Sally is peeved when she sees Claire showing two prospective buyers round her house.
News of the break-in quickly spreads, prompting the couple who had their sights set on Claire's home to pull out of the deal, and Tina's dad Joe (Reece Dinsdale) pays a visit.
